text:
incident-bot: 🚨 GPU queue length exceeded threshold on customer-cluster-42 (private VPC). Autoscaler failed to add nodes: hit provider quota or boot timeout. Queue growth observed for ~12m, throttling active.

Alex M.: paging oncall. I’m taking first touch. can someone confirm customer impact? which tenants are on that cluster?

Priya K.: @Alex M. I see high queue for the gpu-inference queue, pod backlog ~480, avg wait ~90s. One enterprise tenant (fintech-corp) has ~30% of requests failing with 429/503. Logs show autoscaler requests to provider but node provisioning stuck in PENDING.

Samir P.: confirmed. provider API returns quota_error for new GPU instances: "Insufficient project quota for NVIDIA_T4_GPUS". Also a few nodes stuck in bootloop, kubelet not registering: image pull timeout reported.

Emily R.: tagging support: I'm DMing the account team about potential customer impact and short-term credits if we need to. For mitigation, do we want to: 1) evict best-effort non-critical pods on that cluster, 2) failover traffic to hosted region for that tenant, or 3) request emergency quota increase?

Alex M.: good list. Priorities: reduce immediate customer errors, avoid further queue growth. Actions now: 1) attempt graceful eviction of low-priority batch pods; 2) scale down non-GPU workloads to free vCPU/memory; 3) try manual node create with smaller GPU flavor if available. Samir, can you trigger evictions and run the node-create attempt?

Samir P.: starting eviction with `kubectl` runbook. Doing selective eviction label: `redwood/priority=best-effort`. command:```bash
kubectl get pods -n default -l redwood/priority=best-effort -o name | xargs -r kubectl delete --grace-period=30
```

Samir P.: also spawning a manual instance via provider console with a different SKU (t4-small-alt). If that fails due to quota, fallback is cross-region burst or hosted.

incident-bot: incident annotated - severity: high; pager duty: oncall escalation to level2 in 10m.

Priya K.: monitoring dashboards: after eviction started, backlog reduced from 480 -> 220 in 8m. Latency still elevated. However autoscaler attempted 3 scale-ups and got `400 QuotaExceeded` on provider side.

Samir P.: manual instance creation succeeded for one node but kubelet failed TLS handshake during bootstrap (cert provider svc timeout). logs:```text
kubelet: E0407 14:02:34.123 kubelet.go:xxx TLS handshake failed: dial tcp 10.0.0.5:443: i/o timeout
```

Alex M.: that explains nodes not joining. ops-bot, any known networking egress issue to provider control plane from that VPC?

ops-bot: detected intermittent NAT gateway saturation in cluster subnet. Egress rate limit spikes around 13:52-14:05 UTC. Suggests bootstrap packets to provider management API were queued/dropped.

Emily R.: so we have two failure modes: provider quota and local network egress bottleneck causing node bootstrap timeouts. For mitigation: bump NAT capacity (if available), open emergency quota request with provider, and enable tenant failover where possible. I'll coordinate with support.

Alex M.: plan and responsibilities:
- Samir: keep evicting best-effort pods and finish bringing manual node to Ready (follow bootstrap logs).
- Priya: monitor queue and customer errors, prepare rollback if failover caused regressions.
- Emily: contact provider account rep for quota bump + open urgent support case, and inform account team.
- I'll prepare a temporary routing rule to send fintech-corp traffic to hosted inference (if they accept).

Samir P.: eviction finished. backlog now 120. Manual node in Ready=1 (partial). Kube-proxy still showing flaps on 2 nodes. Will capture kubelet bootstrap logs and open an SRE page if it stalls.

Priya K.: fintech-corp reported reduced errors after partial failover; still seeing increased latencies. I've started a targeted canary failover: route 10% of their traffic to hosted, monitor quality.

Alex M.: update on paging: level2 oncall (Samir) is on it. If we can't stabilize in 30m, we escalate to infra-eng for NAT capacity change.

incident-bot: note added - post-incident review required. collect: autoscaler logs, provider quota response headers, NAT metrics, kubelet bootstrap traces, tenant error rates.

Emily R.: provider responded to support case: emergency quota increase requested; ETA 2-3 hours unless account rep pushes it. They suggested creating preemptible GPU instances as alternate flavor; that would reduce cost but may impact reliability. Need product signoff for tenant failover to preemptible.

Alex M.: product signoff not needed for emergency routing to hosted; preemptible use needs opt-in. For now, keep preemptible as last resort.

Samir P.: small update: NAT gateway upgrade is possible via console. Doing it now — should increase egress throughput. Running `kubectl get nodes` repeatedly to watch join events.

Samir P.: NAT change applied. Seeing steady Successful bootstraps: new node count increased to 3, all Ready. Queue falling to ~40. Customer errors dropping.

Priya K.: good recovery signal. I'll keep canary at 10% until everything stabilizes for 30m. Emily, keep provider case open until quota resolved permanently.

Emily R.: will keep case active. Filing internal incident ticket for follow-up: add monitoring for NAT saturation, autoscaler retry backoff tuning, and provider-quotas runbook.

Alex M.: thanks team. After-action items:
- postmortem draft (owner: Alex) w/in 48h
- runbook updates (owner: Samir) - include manual NAT bump and alternate SKU flow
- product/customer comms (owner: Emily) - notify fintech-corp SLA team

Priya K.: adding link to logs and dashboards in the incident ticket. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: incident resolved -> mitigation successful, severity downgraded to medium. Please attach notes to the incident in the tracker.

Alex M.: closing thread for now. If any regressions, re-open this thread or DM oncall. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
